# Psalm 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

**2** Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You gave me relief when I was in distress. Be gracious to me and hear my prayer.

**3** O sons of men, how long shall my honor be turned to shame? How long will you love what is worthless and seek after lies? Selah.

**4** But know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.

**5** Tremble and do not sin; reflect in your hearts on your beds and be still. Selah.

**6** Offer right sacrifices and put your trust in the LORD.

**7** Many are saying, "Who will show us any good?" Lift up the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.

**8** You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and new wine abound.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **4:2**: 'God of my righteousness' — God is the source and guarantor of the psalmist's right standing, not human merit.

- **4:7**: The 'light of Your face' echoes the Aaronic blessing (Numbers 6:25-26). Divine favor is imaged as radiance.

— LOGOS
